topic: Part 5 Test 4 (SAA African Cell Field Strength) — post-patch verification of ISS-2694 three minor prose fixes
our_argument_summary: Test 4 argues the dome's SAA field-strength prediction is non-discriminating (linear extrapolation from CHAOS-7 globe data; both models predict continued weakening), and the EXP-609 paragraph adds that the dome's one genuinely discriminating SAA claim to date (PRED-073, >=0.3 deg/month western-cell drift) falsified on the dome's own rule and was never scored. The ISS-2694 patches adjusted three phrasings: evidentiary weight moved from the SHA hash to the registration date; 'exactly one SAA claim' scoped 'to date'; the pending-on-own-page claim datestamped 'as of 2026-06-11'.

verification_of_patches.ISS-2694 fix 1 (hash-committed phrasing): FIXED. Now reads 'it was genuinely prospective — registered before the window opened (2026-04-04, and hash-committed), with an explicit falsification rule'. Evidentiary weight rests on the registration date; the hash is parenthetical credit. Consistent with our Timestamp Error tab's position that content hashes prove integrity, not temporal priority. Reads naturally.
verification_of_patches.ISS-2694 fix 2 (exactly-one scoping): FIXED. Now reads 'the dome registered exactly one SAA claim to date that genuinely diverged from standard physics' — the 'to date' hedge protects against a future PRED-R001 adjudication flip exactly as c1 recommended.
verification_of_patches.ISS-2694 fix 3 (as-of datestamp): FIXED. Now reads 'the entry still sits as pending on its own predictions page (as of 2026-06-11)' — dated, so it can no longer go stale silently; 6.15 cross-link retained as the canonical live tracker.

holes_found.description: WRONG-PAPER DOI ATTRIBUTION (pre-existing prose in the same Test 4 block, caught in this run's citation sweep — NOT introduced by the ISS-2694 patch): the paragraph 'The globe does NOT predict stability' cites 'CHAOS-7 (Finlay et al., 2020)' with href https://doi.org/10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x. Crossref lookup this run: 10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x is Alken, Thebault et al., 'International Geomagnetic Reference Field: the thirteenth generation' (IGRF-13) — NOT the CHAOS-7 paper and not by Finlay as lead. The correct CHAOS-7 DOI, 10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9 ('The CHAOS-7 geomagnetic field model and observed changes in the South Atlantic Anomaly', Finlay, Kloss et al. — verified via Crossref this run), is already used correctly in the PRED-073 paragraph later in the same test. Wrong-DOI defects are this review's named failure class (WIN-008/009/014 precedent); a defender can quote it: 'their citation for CHAOS-7 resolves to a different paper by different authors.' Severity 'major' per guidelines ('citing the wrong paper'); mitigations: the wrongly-linked paper is itself a legitimate mainstream geomagnetic model reference supporting the same sentence, and the fix is a one-attribute href swap.
holes_found.recommendation: Swap the href in that sentence to https://doi.org/10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9, OR relabel the link 'IGRF-13 (Alken et al., 2021)' and attach it to the IGRF clause instead (note the sentence currently names IGRF-14, so the cleaner fix is the href swap to the true Finlay CHAOS-7 DOI). Check docs/index.html is regenerated from sections.json after the edit (build drift precedent PRED-073/commit 9f6fe08).

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's PRED-073 deserves the credit the paragraph gives it: data/predictions.json:PRED-073 confirms registration_date 2026-04-04 (before the April-May window), an explicit dome_falsification rule ('drifts <0.1deg westward or reverses direction'), and is_genuinely_prospective:true — the only SAA entry in the catalog with that combination (verified against the catalog this run).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The same catalog record shows our_verdict:'falsified' and author_status:'dome_silent': annualized >=0.3deg/month is ~3.65deg/yr vs the CHAOS-7-derived 0.282 +/- 0.030 deg/yr secular rate (data/predictions.json:PRED-073.detail_reasoning; ratio 12.77, prose says '12-13x' — recomputed this run), the window closed 2026-05-31, and the dome's predictions page still lists the entry as pending (as of 2026-06-11, per the datestamped prose and the chg-20260610 poller heartbeat cited in c1). A genuinely risky claim that misses by an order of magnitude and is never scored strengthens, not weakens, Test 4's verdict.

advocate_mode.best_defense: "The reviewers' Test 4 leans on CHAOS-7 as the gold standard, yet their own CHAOS-7 citation resolves to the IGRF-13 paper by different authors — if citation rigor is the standard we're judged by, it cuts both ways. On substance: our PRED-073 cited CHAOS-7 as its verification source in good faith; the reviewers themselves concede no published CHAOS release covers April-May 2026, so calling it 'falsified' before observational data exists is premature — 'pending' is the honest status, which is exactly what our page shows."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Leg 1 (citation tu-quoque) dies with the one-attribute href fix in holes_found[0]. Leg 2 (premature falsification) is already pre-empted in the prose by the honest caveat sentence — the secular rate is constrained to ~0.024deg/month against a >=0.3deg/month claim, a 12x margin no plausible data revision closes; the paragraph says exactly this. No text change needed for leg 2.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: The PRED-073 paragraph's hash phrasing now matches the Timestamp Error tab's position (hashes prove integrity, not priority) — the c1 inconsistency is resolved. 'Exactly one SAA claim to date' checked against the catalog: PRED-R001 (separation >=57deg by 2030) remains assessed trend-extrapolation, PRED-R002 is the non-discriminating field-strength entry Test 4 itself covers; no WIN row contradicts the 'exactly one ... to date' scoping. WIN-023's row (re-reviewed this same run, batch position 1) makes no SAA-drift claims that interact.

summary_for_decider: All three ISS-2694 fixes verified landed and reading naturally; no regressions; all c1 holes closed (carry-over empty). ONE NEW MAJOR: pre-existing wrong-paper DOI in Test 4's 'globe does NOT predict stability' paragraph — 'CHAOS-7 (Finlay et al., 2020)' links to 10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x which is Alken et al. IGRF-13; correct CHAOS-7 DOI 10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9 is already used later in the same test. One-attribute href swap; remember docs/index.html rebuild. Batch aborted per Step 8a(d) on the severity upgrade (this was batch item 2 of 2; no items deferred).
deeper_analysis: Verification pass on queue item 521 (class verification, batch position 2 behind WIN-023.c7/qid 520). The three ISS-2694 phrasing fixes all landed exactly as the c1 recommendations specified, and the paragraph's quantitative spine (12-13x, 0.024deg/month, 3.65deg/yr, dates) re-verified clean against data/predictions.json:PRED-073. The batch's citation sweep — re-running the DOI checks c1 could not complete (its doi.org fetch redirect was cancelled) — surfaced the wrong-paper attribution: the CHAOS-7 label and Finlay byline are attached to the IGRF-13 DOI. c1 had marked 01252-9 'unchecked, no discrepancy suspected' and never examined the earlier paragraph's 01288-x link because its scope was the EXP-609 paragraph; this is the known gap of narrow verification scopes, and exactly the defect class (wrong DOIs: WIN-008/009/014) this review treats as reputationally loaded. Per Step 8a(d) the major finding obliges marking the batch aborted; as this was the final queue item, no work was deferred. Severity calibration considered: the wrongly-linked paper supports the same sentence (IGRF-13 also predicts continued SAA deepening), arguing for moderate — but the severity guide explicitly names 'citing the wrong paper' as major, and the tu-quoque exposure in a section whose whole argument is citation rigor makes major the right call.
